subject: UBERON:0002048
object: Exchanges oxygen and carbon dioxide between alveolar gas and pulmonary capillary blood by passive diffusion across the blood-gas barrier

sources.citation: West JB & Luks AM, West's Respiratory Physiology: The Essentials, 11th ed.

population: healthy adult, both sexes, at rest, sea level
limitations: A statement of the organ's principal function. Ventilation, perfusion and diffusion each have their own limiting conditions, none represented here.

population: healthy adult, both sexes, at rest, sea level
limitations: A rounded reference value for quiet breathing. Tidal volume varies with body size, posture and metabolic demand; ~7 mL/kg is the size-scaled form and is not represented as a separate claim.

conditions.notes: quiet breathing, upright, breathing air at sea level

subject: UBERON:0002048

sources.citation: OpenStax College, Anatomy & Physiology 1e, OpenStax CNX (CC BY 3.0)
Hall JE & Hall ME, Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed.

population: healthy adult, both sexes, at rest, sea level
limitations: Corrected by the verification pass (D-033). The first version recorded 14 as "the midpoint of the commonly cited 12-16 range"; OpenStax states "12 to 18 breaths per minute" for adults, so the range was wrong and the midpoint with it. Sources genuinely differ on the upper bound — Guyton gives 12-16, OpenStax 12-18 — and the recorded value is the midpoint of the wider, openly checkable range. The range is the honest form; a single value is a limitation of the claim record, not of the biology.

subject: UBERON:0007196

sources.citation: West JB & Luks AM, West's Respiratory Physiology: The Essentials, 11th ed.

population: healthy adult, both sexes, at rest, sea level
limitations: The conducting-airway volume that does not participate in gas exchange, approximated as 2.2 mL per kg body weight. Physiological dead space is a different quantity, measured by a different method, and is not this value.

conditions.notes: Fowler's single-breath nitrogen washout; scales with body weight

subject: UBERON:0002048

sources.citation: Hall JE & Hall ME, Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed.

population: healthy adult, both sexes, at rest, sea level
limitations: Functional residual capacity: the volume remaining after a quiet expiration, where inward lung recoil balances outward chest-wall recoil. Posture-dependent; supine values are substantially lower and are not represented.

conditions.notes: upright, end of a quiet expiration; helium dilution or body plethysmography

subject: UBERON:0002048

sources.citation: Hall JE & Hall ME, Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed.

population: healthy adult male, 20-40 years, at rest, sea level
limitations: Total lung capacity for the stated population. Scales with standing height more strongly than with sex alone; height is not represented in the population field, which is a limit of this record.

subject: UBERON:0002048

sources.citation: Hall JE & Hall ME, Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed.

population: healthy adult female, 20-40 years, at rest, sea level
limitations: Total lung capacity for the stated population. Differs from the male reference by roughly 30%, largely through body size. This is a different population, not a competing measurement.

population: healthy adult, both sexes, at rest, sea level
limitations: The classic textbook estimate of the alveolar gas-exchange surface. Design-based stereology gives roughly twice this figure; the disagreement is methodological and unresolved, so both are retained.

conditions.notes: fixed lung, light-microscopic morphometry; the fixation and shrinkage assumptions are where this diverges from the stereological figure

subject: UBERON:0002048

Ochs M et al., The number of alveoli in the human lung, Am J Respir Crit Care Med 169:120-124, 2004

population: healthy adult, both sexes, at rest, sea level
limitations: Morphometric estimate from design-based stereology on fixed lungs. Depends on fixation and on the assumed shrinkage correction, which is the substance of the disagreement with the classic figure.

conditions.notes: perfusion-fixed lung, design-based stereology with shrinkage correction

subject: UBERON:0002048

sources.citation: Ochs M et al., The number of alveoli in the human lung, Am J Respir Crit Care Med 169:120-124, 2004

population: healthy adult, both sexes, at rest, sea level
limitations: Mean alveolar number from design-based stereology in six adult lungs (range 274-790 million). The mean is recorded because the record holds one value; the spread is wider than the mean is precise, and the value should not be read as a population constant.

conditions.notes: perfusion-fixed lungs, design-based stereology, physical disector; n=6

subject: UBERON:0001103
object: The principal muscle of quiet inspiration: contraction flattens the dome, increasing thoracic volume and lowering intrapleural pressure

sources.citation: West JB & Luks AM, West's Respiratory Physiology: The Essentials, 11th ed.

population: healthy adult, both sexes, at rest, sea level
limitations: Accessory muscles contribute increasingly with effort and are not represented. The claim is about quiet breathing only.

subject: UBERON:0001103

sources.citation: West JB & Luks AM, West's Respiratory Physiology: The Essentials, 11th ed.

population: healthy adult, both sexes, at rest, sea level
limitations: Approximate share of resting tidal volume attributable to diaphragmatic descent. Inferred from the commonly cited 60-80% range; posture and abdominal compliance both move it.

conditions.notes: supine and upright quiet breathing; the share moves with posture

subject: UBERON:0001103
object: Innervated by the phrenic nerve, arising from cervical roots C3-C5

sources.citation: Hall JE & Hall ME, Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed.

population: healthy adult, both sexes, at rest, sea level
limitations: A structural fact of gross anatomy stated at nerve-root resolution. Contributions from C3 and C5 vary between individuals.

subject: UBERON:0007196

sources.citation: West JB & Luks AM, West's Respiratory Physiology: The Essentials, 11th ed.

population: healthy adult, both sexes, at rest, sea level
limitations: Weibel symmetric-branching model: airway generations from trachea to alveolar sacs. Real branching is asymmetric, and the count is a property of the model rather than of any particular lung.

conditions.notes: Weibel symmetric-branching model of a resin cast; a model property, not a measurement of one lung

subject: UBERON:0007196

sources.citation: West JB & Luks AM, West's Respiratory Physiology: The Essentials, 11th ed.

population: healthy adult, both sexes, at rest, sea level
limitations: Generations 0-16 conduct without gas exchange; 17-23 are the respiratory zone. Same model dependence as the total generation count.

conditions.notes: as above — the conducting/respiratory boundary is a feature of the same model

subject: UBERON:0002182
object: The right main bronchus is wider, shorter and more vertical than the left, which is why inhaled material reaches the right lung preferentially

sources.citation: Hall JE & Hall ME, Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed.

population: healthy adult, both sexes, at rest, sea level
limitations: A structural asymmetry with a well-known consequence. Stated as anatomy; no clinical inference is drawn from it here.

subject: UBERON:0002048

sources.citation: West JB & Luks AM, West's Respiratory Physiology: The Essentials, 11th ed.

population: healthy adult, both sexes, at rest, sea level
limitations: Diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide at rest — the standard proxy for the blood-gas barrier's conductance, because CO uptake is diffusion-limited. Rises severalfold with exercise; the resting value is not a maximum.

conditions.notes: single-breath carbon monoxide method, at rest, seated

subject: UBERON:0002048

sources.citation: Hall JE & Hall ME, Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed.

population: healthy adult, both sexes, at rest, sea level
limitations: Derived as (tidal volume - dead space) x respiratory rate from the reference values above. Inferred rather than measured, and it inherits every approximation in its inputs — which is why it is EVC-5 and its components are EVC-4.

conditions.notes: derived, not measured: computed from the resting tidal volume, dead space and rate recorded here

subject: UBERON:0002048

sources.citation: Gehr P, Bachofen M, Weibel ER, The normal human lung: ultrastructure and morphometric estimation of diffusion capacity, Respir Physiol 32:121-140, 1978

population: healthy adult, both sexes, at rest, sea level
limitations: Harmonic mean thickness of the tissue barrier between alveolar gas and capillary blood in its thinnest regions. The barrier is not uniform, and a single thickness is a deliberate simplification of a distribution.

conditions.notes: perfusion-fixed lung, electron-microscopic morphometry; harmonic mean over the thin portions of the barrier

subject: UBERON:0002048
object: Receives the entire cardiac output, unlike any other organ, so pulmonary blood flow equals systemic blood flow in the steady state

sources.citation: West JB & Luks AM, West's Respiratory Physiology: The Essentials, 11th ed.

population: healthy adult, both sexes, at rest, sea level
limitations: True in the steady state and at the whole-organ level. Bronchial circulation and physiological shunt are small exceptions not represented here.
